The intended pairing: position 18 pairs with 88, position 362 pairs with 16's partner... wait, the outermost stem [16,364] has opens at 16,17 and closes 363,364. Then [18,19] is the next stem closing at... let me check. Stem at opens 18,19 closes at 87,88. Stem at opens 27,28 closes at 79,80? No — 27,28 closes at 78,79.

The spurious pairs show the MFE prefers 18-362 (long range) over 18-88 (intended). Both are GC. The reason: long-range with stronger stacking context.

To break this, I should make the OUTER stems weaker (AU) and inner stems stronger, OR break complementarity between distant stems. Since the outer multiloop [16,364] must close, I need its stem (16-17 / 363-364) strong, but the NEXT layer (18-19 / 87-88) shouldn't pair with the far end (361-362).

Key realization: stems [18,19]→[87,88] and [310,311]→[361,362] are both strong GC and complementary, so they cross-pair (18-362). If I make them non-complementary (one GC, one AU, or one GG one UU), they won't cross-pair.

Let me assign stem pairs so that NO two distant stems are mutually complementary. Simplest: make every stem use the SAME orientation GC (G on 5' open, C on 3' close) — then opens are all G and closes are all C, so open-open and close-close never pair, but open of one + close of another = G-C = pairs! That's the problem.

Better: alternate so that half the stems are GC (open G, close C) and half CG (open C, close G). Then open-G stems can pair with close-C stems of OTHER GC stems. To fully prevent cross-pairing, stems in the same multiloop should share orientation so their opens are identical (G,G) → can't pair with each other's closes (C,C)... no, G pairs with C.

The real fix: make the LOOP regions (the 15-nt) not contain G/C, so the only G/C are in stems. Then cross-pairing only happens between stem G's and stem C's. To prevent stem_i_open pairing with stem_j_close, I want stem_i and stem_j to NOT be G...C complementary.
